relations.evidence: both Joseph and Alexander obtained cadetships at the East India Company's Addiscombe Seminary (1829–31)

relations.subject: Alexander Cunningham
relations.evidence: He was in daily communication with Prinsep during 1837 and 1838 and became his intimate friend, confidant and pupil.

relations.subject: Alexander Cunningham
relations.evidence: He had conducted excavations at Sarnath in 1837 along with Frederick Charles Maisey

relations.subject: Alexander Cunningham
relations.evidence: Lord Canning, then Viceroy of India, appointed Cunningham as an archaeological surveyor to the Government of India. He held this position from 1861 to 1865

relations.subject: Alexander Cunningham
relations.evidence: and he founded and organised what later became the Archaeological Survey of India.

relations.subject: Alexander Cunningham
relations.evidence: In 1870, Lord Mayo re-established the Archaeological Survey of India, with Cunningham as its director-general from 1 January 1871... He retired from the Archaeological Survey on 30 September 1885

relations.subject: J. D. Beglar
relations.evidence: He produced twenty-four reports, thirteen as author and the rest under his supervision by others such as J. D. Beglar.
